propertyTaxRate.note: Tax Foundation 'Property Taxes by State' table (published Mar 16, 2026): Maryland 0.92% for 2024 (0.95% for 2023), computed as total real taxes paid / total owner-occupied home value from Census ACS B25082 and B25090. File value 1.09% is 0.17 pp above the 2024 figure. The file figure appears to come from an older median-based series; decide which series the tool standardizes on before changing it.

programs.name: Disabled Veteran Exemption

details.current: 100% disabled veterans: $5,000 assessed value exemption on primary residence.
details.correct: Full exemption of the dwelling house from state, county and municipal property tax for a veteran with a permanent 100% service-connected disability (Tax-Property §7-208); unremarried surviving spouse keeps it.
details.quote: a dwelling house is exempt from property tax if: (1) the dwelling house is owned by: (i) a disabled veteran ... (ii) a surviving spouse

survivingSpouse.quote: 'Surviving spouse' means an individual who has not remarried and who: (i) is the surviving spouse of a disabled veteran; (ii) ... died in the line of duty; or (iii) receives Dependency and Indemnity Compensation

ratingRequired.quote: has been declared by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to have a permanent 100% service connected disability

ptRequired.quote: a permanent 100% service connected disability ... reasonably certain to continue for the life of the veteran

type.quote: The page contains no dollar cap; 'a dwelling house is exempt from property tax'

programs.note: The statute text contains no 'unemployability' wording; the SDAT application form accepts 'permanent unemployability' as qualifying, so TDIU-at-100% veterans should check with SDAT rather than rely on the statute alone. No 2025 or 2026 amendment to §7-208 was found on mgaleg.maryland.gov. The $5,000 figure in `details` is wrong and should be replaced.

programs.name: County Credits

incomeLimit.quote: the disabled veteran's federal adjusted gross income for the immediately preceding taxable year does not exceed $100,000

correct.appliesTo: county or municipal tax only, where adopted
county or municipal tax only, where adopted; not available if the veteran qualifies under §7-208

tiers.quote: 50% of the county or municipal corporation property tax ... if the disabled veteran's service-connected disability rating is at least 75% and the disabled veteran does not qualify for a property tax exemption under § 7-208

survivingSpouse.quote: the governing body of a county or municipal corporation may, by law, continue to provide the property tax credit under this section to the surviving spouse of the disabled veteran

summary.current: 25% of county/municipal tax at 50-74% rating, 50% at 75-99%
summary.correct: Same tiers, plus: FAGI cap $100,000; the 50% tier is for veterans at 75%+ who do NOT qualify under §7-208 (so a non-permanent 100% rating lands here); surviving-spouse continuation is a local option.
summary.quote: 25% of the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on the dwelling house if the disabled veteran's service-connected disability rating is at least 50% but not more than 74%

programs.note: Statute confirms the credit is a local option (Baltimore City, counties, municipalities 'may grant, by law'), so continuing to list it without adding it to the dollar estimate is right. The $100,000 FAGI cap is missing from the row.

sources.title: Md. Code, Tax-Property §7-208 (dwelling house of disabled veteran or surviving spouse)
Md. Code, Tax-Property §9-265 (local-option disabled veteran credit)
SDAT Application for Exemption for Disabled Veterans (Rev Feb 2025)
Tax Foundation, Property Taxes by State and County, 2026 (2024 ACS data)

summary: The §7-208 exemption is a complete exemption with surviving-spouse coverage; the row's $5,000 `details` string and survivingSpouse:false are both wrong. The §9-265 county credit tiers are right but the row omits the $100,000 FAGI cap and the rule that the 50% tier is only for veterans who do not qualify under §7-208; the effective tax rate is 0.17 pp above the Tax Foundation 2024 figure.
